spec.name: Earnings drift v30
spec.notes: Post-earnings drift on the reported surprise.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.97 to 1.93 (change -0.04).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.97 to 0.19. Changed by strict mode: fields eps_reported.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.97 (as submitted, 10 bps: 1.97); it breaks even at 195.3 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.97 against 1.97 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.85 against 1.97 in research, a gap of +1.12.
The best year gives 17% of total P&L (year 6) and calm regimes give 91%; Sharpe is 2.89 in calm and 0.52 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.01, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 1.99 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.09 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.49).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.97 to as low as 1.63 (as low as 1.76 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (22 days) give 30% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 18% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
